name: Frontal bone
location: Forehead and front of the cranial vault.
clues: Forms the forehead above the eyes.
Lies anterior to the coronal suture.
function: Forms part of the protective cranium and the roofs of the eye sockets.

name: Parietal bones
location: Paired bones of the roof and upper sides of the cranium.
clues: Meet in the midline at the sagittal suture.
Lie between the frontal and occipital bones.
function: Form much of the cranial roof and side walls.

name: Sagittal suture
location: Midline junction between the right and left parietal bones.
clues: Runs front to back along the top of the skull.
Separates the two parietal bones.
function: Joins the paired parietal bones.

name: Coronal suture
location: Junction between the frontal bone and both parietal bones.
clues: Runs across the skull behind the forehead.
Marks the front edge of the parietal bones.
function: Joins the frontal and parietal bones.

name: Lambdoid suture
location: Posterior junction of the parietal bones with the occipital bone.
clues: Look at the back of the skull.
Forms an inverted V-like boundary above the occipital bone.
function: Joins the parietal bones to the occipital bone.

name: Squamous suture
location: Lateral junction between a parietal bone and a temporal bone.
clues: Arches above the ear region.
Separates the upper parietal bone from the temporal bone below.
function: Joins temporal and parietal bones.

name: Temporal bones
location: Lower lateral walls and part of the base of the cranium.
clues: Surround the external ear openings.
Carry the mastoid and styloid processes.
function: Help form the cranial base and house structures of hearing and balance.

name: Zygomatic process of temporal bone
location: Forward-projecting part of the temporal bone above the mandibular fossa.
clues: A narrow projection extending toward the cheek.
Forms the posterior contribution to the zygomatic arch.
function: Contributes to the zygomatic arch.

name: Zygomatic arch
location: Bony bridge on the side of the face between the cheek and temporal region.
clues: An arch above the side of the lower jaw.
The whole arch is larger than the temporal bone’s zygomatic process alone.
function: Forms the prominent bony arch of the cheek region.

name: Mandibular fossa
location: Depression on the temporal bone inferior to its zygomatic process.
clues: A socket-like depression just anterior to the external auditory meatus.
Receives the upper joint surface of the mandible.
function: Articulates with the mandible at the jaw joint.

name: External auditory meatus
location: Ear-canal opening on the lateral temporal bone.
clues: Round or oval opening behind the mandibular fossa.
Visible on the outside of the skull.
function: Forms the bony part of the passage toward the eardrum.

name: Styloid process of temporal bone
location: Slender projection extending inferiorly from the temporal bone.
clues: Thin and pointed, unlike the thick mastoid process.
Look below the external auditory meatus.
function: Provides attachment for muscles and ligaments in the head and neck.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

name: Mastoid process
location: Rounded projection posterior and inferior to the external auditory meatus.
clues: A large blunt bump behind the ear opening.
Much thicker than the neighboring styloid process.
function: Provides muscle attachment and contains small air spaces.

name: Carotid canal
location: Passage through the temporal bone at the cranial base.
clues: Find its external opening on the inferior skull.
It lies anterior to the jugular foramen.
function: Provides a route for the internal carotid artery into the cranium.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

name: Jugular foramen
location: Opening at the junction of the temporal and occipital bones.
clues: Visible at the cranial base, lateral to the foramen magnum.
Posterior to the carotid canal opening.
function: Provides a passage for major venous drainage and several cranial nerves.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

name: Internal auditory (acoustic) meatus
location: Opening on the internal surface of the temporal bone.
clues: Visible from inside the cranial cavity.
Do not confuse it with the ear opening on the outside of the skull.
function: Transmits nerves associated with the face, hearing, and balance.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

name: Occipital bone
location: Back and lower base of the cranium.
clues: Below the lambdoid suture on the posterior skull.
Contains the foramen magnum at its base.
function: Forms the back of the cranium and surrounds the opening for the spinal cord.

name: Foramen magnum
location: Large midline opening in the inferior occipital bone.
clues: The largest opening at the skull base.
Occipital condyles lie beside it.
function: Provides the passage between the cranial cavity and vertebral canal.

name: Occipital condyles
location: Paired smooth surfaces beside the foramen magnum.
clues: Oval joint surfaces on either side of the large skull-base opening.
Located anterolateral to the foramen magnum.
function: Articulate with the atlas (C1).

name: Sphenoid bone
location: Central portion of the cranial base, posterior to the frontal bone.
clues: A complex butterfly-like bone when isolated.
Contains the central sella turcica.
function: Connects with surrounding skull bones and contributes to the cranial base and orbits.

name: Sella turcica
location: Saddle-like region on the superior central sphenoid.
clues: Look for the central saddle on an internal skull view.
It lies posterior to the optic canals.
function: Contains the depression that accommodates the pituitary gland.

name: Optic canal
location: Paired canals in the sphenoid near the anterior cranial base.
clues: Small paired openings near the front of the sphenoid’s central portion.
Best seen with the cranial roof removed.
function: Provides a passage for the optic nerve.

name: Ethmoid bone
location: Deep midline skull bone between the orbits and above the nasal cavity.
clues: Small and complex compared with surrounding cranial bones.
Its superior surface includes the cribriform plate.
function: Contributes to the nasal cavity, medial orbital walls, and cranial base.

name: Cribriform plate
location: Perforated superior surface of the ethmoid bone.
clues: A sieve-like plate visible in the anterior cranial floor.
Its many small holes are a useful distinguishing feature.
function: Forms part of the nasal roof and transmits olfactory nerve fibers.

name: Maxillae
location: Paired upper-jaw bones beneath the orbits.
clues: Carry the upper teeth.
Form much of the upper jaw and part of each orbit’s floor.
function: Support the upper teeth and contribute to the palate and orbital floors.

name: Mandible
location: Lower jaw.
clues: A U-shaped body with an ascending portion on each side.
Carries the lower teeth.
function: Forms the movable lower jaw.

name: Coronoid process of mandible
location: Anterior superior projection on each ascending side of the mandible.
clues: The pointed anterior projection at the top of the mandibular ramus.
It is anterior to the jaw’s rounded joint process.
function: Provides a major attachment for a chewing muscle.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

name: Hyoid bone
location: Superior neck, below the mandible.
clues: Small horseshoe-shaped bone.
Suspended in the neck without directly articulating with another bone.
function: Supports tongue and neck muscle attachments and helps with swallowing.

name: Sternum
location: Midline anterior thorax.
clues: Flat breastbone in the center of the chest.
Its superior portion is the manubrium and inferior tip is the xiphoid process.
function: Forms the anterior support of the thoracic cage.

name: Manubrium
location: Superior, broad portion of the sternum.
clues: Broad upper segment of the breastbone.
The clavicles meet its upper lateral sides.
function: Forms the superior part of the sternum and articulates with the clavicles.

name: Xiphoid process
location: Small inferior tip of the sternum.
clues: Lowest part of the breastbone.
Smaller and more variable in shape than the manubrium.
function: Forms the inferior end of the sternum and provides soft-tissue attachment.

name: Cervical vertebrae
location: Seven vertebrae in the neck.
clues: Look for a transverse foramen on each side.
Typical examples are smaller than lumbar vertebrae; C1 and C2 are specialized.
function: Support the head and allow neck movement.

name: Thoracic vertebrae
location: Twelve vertebrae in the thoracic region.
clues: Have joint surfaces for ribs.
Typical middle examples have a long spinous process directed downward.
function: Articulate with ribs and contribute to the thoracic cage.
sourceNote: The lab export, page 38, calls all thoracic vertebral foramina triangular. This is not used as an identification rule; typical thoracic foramina are more circular, and regional variation exists.

name: Lumbar vertebrae
location: Five large vertebrae of the lower back.
clues: Large, thick vertebral body.
Short, broad spinous process and no transverse foramina.
function: Bear substantial body weight in the lower back.

name: Sacrum
location: Posterior pelvis between the two coxal bones.
clues: Triangular bone formed from fused vertebrae.
Broad superior end and tapered inferior end.
function: Transfers weight from the vertebral column to the pelvic girdle.

name: Coccyx
location: Small terminal segment inferior to the sacrum.
clues: Much smaller than the sacrum.
A short sequence of fused or partly fused terminal segments.
function: Forms the terminal part of the vertebral column and provides soft-tissue attachment.

name: Atlas (C1)
location: First cervical vertebra, directly beneath the skull.
clues: Ring-like shape without a vertebral body.
Lacks the typical spinous process.
function: Articulates with the occipital condyles and supports the head.

name: Axis (C2)
location: Second cervical vertebra, immediately inferior to the atlas.
clues: Recognize the dens projecting upward.
Has a vertebral body, unlike the atlas.
function: Provides the pivot for rotation of the atlas and head.

name: Dens of axis
location: Superior projection from the body of the axis.
clues: Tooth-like projection pointing upward.
Fits inside the ring of the atlas.
function: Acts as the pivot for head rotation.

name: Transverse foramen
location: Opening in each transverse process of a cervical vertebra.
clues: Paired side openings, separate from the large central opening.
A useful marker for the cervical region.
function: Provides a passage for vessels in the cervical region.

name: Spinous process of vertebra
location: Midline posterior projection of a typical vertebra.
clues: Single projection toward the back.
Distinguish it from the paired lateral transverse processes.
function: Provides attachment for muscles and ligaments.

name: Transverse process of vertebra
location: Paired lateral projections of a vertebra.
clues: Project to the sides rather than the posterior midline.
Cervical examples contain transverse foramina.
function: Provide muscle and ligament attachment; thoracic examples may also articulate with ribs.

name: Lamina of vertebra
location: Posterior plate of the vertebral arch on either side of the spinous process.
clues: A short bony bridge leading toward the spinous process.
Forms part of the posterior wall around the vertebral opening.
function: Helps enclose the vertebral canal.

name: Body of vertebra (centrum)
location: Anterior weight-bearing portion of a typical vertebra.
clues: Large block-like portion opposite the spinous process.
Absent as a separate body in the atlas.
function: Bears weight and meets adjacent vertebral bodies through discs.

name: Rib
location: Curved bones extending around the thorax from the thoracic vertebrae.
clues: Long, curved and flattened.
The costal groove follows part of the inner surface near the inferior border.
sideTip: Orient the vertebral end posteriorly and the costal groove inferiorly before deciding the side.
function: Helps protect thoracic organs and supports the chest wall.

name: Costal groove
location: Groove on the internal surface near the inferior border of a typical rib.
clues: Follow the lower inside edge of the rib shaft.
It is a groove, not one of the smooth joint surfaces.
function: Shelters blood vessels and a nerve along the rib.

name: Scapula
location: Flat triangular bone on the posterior shoulder.
clues: The prominent spine is on the posterior surface.
The glenoid cavity faces laterally.
sideTip: Place the spine posteriorly and the glenoid cavity laterally; the inferior angle points down.
function: Links the upper limb with the shoulder girdle.

name: Glenoid cavity
location: Shallow socket on the lateral angle of the scapula.
clues: Oval depression facing away from the trunk.
Smaller and shallower than the pelvic acetabulum.
function: Articulates with the head of the humerus.

name: Coracoid process
location: Anterior projection from the superior scapula.
clues: Hook-like projection pointing forward.
Different from the broader acromion, which continues from the spine.
function: Provides attachment for muscles and ligaments around the shoulder.

name: Acromion
location: Broad lateral extension of the scapular spine.
clues: Forms the high outer part of the shoulder.
Follow the scapular spine laterally to find it.
function: Articulates with the acromial end of the clavicle.

name: Spine of scapula
location: Prominent ridge across the posterior scapula.
clues: Divides the posterior surface into two fossae.
Extends laterally toward the acromion.
function: Provides muscle attachment and separates the posterior fossae.

name: Supraspinous fossa
location: Posterior scapular depression superior to the spine.
clues: Smaller of the two major posterior fossae.
Supra means above: look above the spine.
function: Provides a surface for shoulder-muscle attachment.

name: Infraspinous fossa
location: Posterior scapular depression inferior to the spine.
clues: Large depression below the scapular spine.
Infra means below.
function: Provides a surface for shoulder-muscle attachment.

name: Clavicle
location: S-shaped bone across the anterior shoulder girdle.
clues: Runs between sternum and scapula.
Its S shape is easiest to see from above.
sideTip: Place the bulky sternal end medially and the flattened acromial end laterally; the medial curve bows anteriorly.
function: Holds the shoulder and upper limb away from the trunk.

name: Sternal end of clavicle
location: Medial end of the clavicle.
clues: The thicker end nearest the midline.
Meets the manubrium.
function: Articulates with the sternum.

name: Acromial end of clavicle
location: Lateral end of the clavicle.
clues: Flatter end near the shoulder.
Meets the scapular acromion.
function: Articulates with the acromion.

name: Humerus
location: Single long bone between shoulder and elbow.
clues: Rounded proximal head and expanded distal end.
Large olecranon fossa on the distal posterior surface.
sideTip: Place the rounded head proximally and medially, with the olecranon fossa facing posteriorly.
function: Forms the upper arm and contributes to shoulder and elbow joints.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Head of humerus
location: Rounded proximal medial surface of the humerus.
clues: Smooth ball-like surface at the shoulder end.
Faces toward the glenoid cavity.
function: Articulates with the scapular glenoid cavity.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Greater tubercle of humerus
location: Large prominence lateral to the proximal humeral head.
clues: Larger of the two proximal tubercles.
Look beside the smooth humeral head.
function: Provides attachment for shoulder muscles.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Lesser tubercle of humerus
location: Smaller prominence on the anterior proximal humerus.
clues: Smaller and more anterior than the greater tubercle.
Separated from it by a groove.
function: Provides attachment for a shoulder muscle.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Deltoid tuberosity
location: Roughened area on the lateral humeral shaft.
clues: A rough projection partway along the shaft.
Below the proximal tubercles.
function: Attachment site for the deltoid muscle.

name: Trochlea of humerus
location: Medial articular region at the distal humerus.
clues: Spool-shaped surface near the elbow.
Medial to the rounder capitulum.
function: Articulates with the trochlear notch of the ulna.

name: Capitulum
location: Lateral articular region at the distal humerus.
clues: Rounded knob-like joint surface.
Lateral to the spool-shaped trochlea.
function: Articulates with the radial head.

name: Olecranon fossa
location: Deep depression on the posterior distal humerus.
clues: Large hollow just superior to the trochlea.
Its posterior position helps orient the humerus.
function: Receives the ulnar olecranon process when the elbow straightens.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Ulna
location: Medial forearm bone in anatomical position.
clues: Large U-shaped proximal end.
Small rounded distal head near the wrist.
sideTip: Point the trochlear notch anteriorly, keep the olecranon proximal, and place the radial articulation laterally.
function: Articulates with the humerus and radius.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Olecranon process
location: Large posterior superior process at the proximal ulna.
clues: Forms the point of the elbow.
Upper lip of the large trochlear notch.
function: Fits into the humeral olecranon fossa during elbow extension.

name: Coronoid process of ulna
location: Anterior projection at the lower margin of the trochlear notch.
clues: Smaller anterior lip beneath the notch.
Do not confuse it with the mandible’s coronoid process.
function: Contributes to the elbow’s bony articulation and stability.

name: Trochlear notch
location: Large curved articular notch at the proximal ulna.
clues: A deep U- or C-shaped curve.
Lies between the olecranon and coronoid processes.
function: Fits around the humeral trochlea.

name: Ulnar head
location: Small rounded distal end of the ulna.
clues: Located at the wrist end, not the elbow end.
Near the ulnar styloid process.
function: Articulates with the distal radius; it does not directly articulate with the carpal bones.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

sourceNote: The lab export, page 48, says the ulnar head articulates with the lunate. This card follows the correction that the distal ulna does not directly articulate with the carpal bones.

name: Styloid process of ulna
location: Small pointed projection beside the distal ulnar head.
clues: A distal spike next to the rounded head.
On the medial side of the forearm.
function: Provides attachment for connective tissues near the wrist.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Radius
location: Lateral forearm bone on the thumb side in anatomical position.
clues: Disc-shaped proximal head.
Much broader at the wrist end than at the elbow end.
sideTip: Place the disc-shaped head proximally, the tuberosity medially, and the distal styloid laterally.
function: Contributes to elbow and wrist joints and rotates with the forearm.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Radial head
location: Disc-shaped proximal end of the radius.
clues: Small round disc at the elbow end.
Different from the distal head of the ulna.
function: Articulates with the humeral capitulum and the proximal ulna.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Radial tuberosity
location: Rough projection just distal to the radial head and neck.
clues: A bump near the elbow end of the radius.
Situated on the medial side.
function: Provides a muscle attachment that helps flex the elbow and turn the forearm.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Styloid process of radius
location: Pointed projection at the lateral distal radius.
clues: A spike at the broad wrist end.
Points toward the thumb side.
function: Provides ligament attachment on the lateral side of the wrist.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

name: Pelvis
location: Bony ring at the base of the trunk.
clues: Both coxal bones together with sacrum and coccyx.
A ring-like assembly, not a single coxal bone.
function: Supports pelvic organs and transfers body weight to the lower limbs.

name: Sacroiliac joints
location: Junctions between the sacrum and the right and left ilia.
clues: One on each side of the sacrum.
At the posterior part of the pelvic ring.
function: Connect the axial skeleton to the pelvic girdle.

name: Coxal bone
location: One side of the pelvic girdle.
clues: Fusion of ilium, ischium, and pubis.
Has an acetabulum laterally and a large obturator foramen inferiorly.
sideTip: Place the acetabulum laterally, the pubis anteriorly, and the broad ilium superiorly.
function: Forms one side of the pelvis and articulates with the femur.

name: Acetabulum
location: Deep lateral socket of the coxal bone.
clues: Round, deep cup above the obturator foramen.
Located where ilium, ischium, and pubis meet.
function: Articulates with the femoral head.

name: Obturator foramen
location: Large opening formed by the pubis and ischium.
clues: Large hole inferior to the acetabulum.
Do not confuse this opening with the acetabular socket.
function: Most of the opening is covered by a membrane in life.

name: Ilium
location: Broad superior part of a coxal bone.
clues: Largest and most superior coxal component.
Its upper rim is the iliac crest.
function: Forms the upper part of the hip bone and meets the sacrum.

name: Iliac crest
location: Superior curved border of the ilium.
clues: Thick upper rim of the broad iliac wing.
The ridge felt when placing hands on hips.
function: Provides attachment for muscles and connective tissue.

name: Greater sciatic notch
location: Large notch on the posterior border of the coxal bone.
clues: Deep posterior indentation above the ischial spine.
Below the posterior ilium.
function: Contributes to a passage between the pelvis and gluteal region when completed by ligaments.

name: Ischium
location: Posteroinferior part of the coxal bone.
clues: Below and behind the acetabulum.
Includes the large ischial tuberosity.
function: Forms the lower posterior hip bone and bears weight during sitting.

name: Ischial tuberosity
location: Thick rough prominence on the inferior ischium.
clues: Large rough sitting-bone prominence.
Posterior and inferior to the obturator foramen.
function: Supports body weight when sitting and provides muscle attachment.

name: Pubis
location: Anterior portion of the coxal bone.
clues: Meets its opposite partner at the anterior midline.
Forms part of the border of the obturator foramen.
function: Forms the anterior part of the pelvic ring.

name: Pubic symphysis
location: Midline joint between the right and left pubic bones.
clues: At the front center of the pelvis.
The joint is above the pubic arch.
function: Unites the pubic bones with fibrocartilage.

name: Pubic arch
location: Arch below the pubic symphysis formed by the inferior pubic regions of both sides.
clues: An inverted V-shaped angle below the midline pubic joint.
Requires both sides of the pelvis to see the whole arch.
function: Forms part of the anterior boundary of the pelvic outlet.

name: Femur
location: Single long bone of the thigh.
clues: Large proximal head on a distinct neck.
Two large distal condyles at the knee.
sideTip: Point the head medially and keep the linea aspera on the posterior shaft.
function: Transfers body weight between the pelvis and tibia.

name: Head of femur
location: Rounded proximal medial end of the femur.
clues: Ball-shaped surface at the end of the neck.
Faces toward the acetabulum.
function: Articulates with the acetabulum of the hip bone.

name: Neck of femur
location: Narrow segment connecting the femoral head to the shaft region.
clues: Constriction between head and trochanters.
Runs obliquely between the head and the upper shaft.
function: Connects the femoral head with the rest of the bone.

name: Greater trochanter
location: Large lateral projection near the proximal femur.
clues: Large bump lateral to the femoral neck.
Much larger than the lesser trochanter.
function: Provides attachment for muscles acting at the hip.

name: Lesser trochanter
location: Smaller posteromedial projection just below the femoral neck.
clues: Small bump below the neck on the posterior medial side.
Best exposed by rotating the femur toward a posterior view.
function: Provides attachment for a major hip-flexor tendon.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

name: Gluteal tuberosity
location: Roughened proximal posterior area of the femoral shaft.
clues: Rough ridge below the greater trochanter.
Proximal to much of the linea aspera.
function: Provides attachment for the gluteus maximus muscle.

name: Linea aspera
location: Long ridge on the posterior femoral shaft.
clues: Runs lengthwise along the back of the femur.
Useful for orienting the bone posteriorly.
function: Provides attachment for several thigh muscles.

name: Medial condyle of femur
location: Distal femoral joint surface on the side nearer the body midline.
clues: One of the two large rounded knee surfaces.
On the same anatomical side as the femoral head.
function: Articulates with the medial side of the tibia.

name: Lateral condyle of femur
location: Distal femoral joint surface farther from the body midline.
clues: The outer of the two large rounded knee surfaces.
Opposite the medial condyle across the posterior notch.
function: Articulates with the lateral side of the tibia.

name: Patella
location: Anterior to the distal femur at the knee.
clues: Small triangular kneecap.
The pointed end faces inferiorly.
sideTip: With the apex inferior and joint surface posterior, the lateral articular facet is usually larger. Facet size varies, so compare the full shape.
function: Protects the front of the knee and improves the leverage of knee extension.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb
Morphometric Analysis of Dry Human Patella and Patellar Facets (2022)

name: Tibia
location: Larger medial bone of the leg between knee and ankle.
clues: Broad proximal end and thick shaft.
Distal medial malleolus forms the inner ankle prominence.
sideTip: Place the tibial tuberosity anteriorly and the medial malleolus toward the body midline.
function: Main weight-bearing bone of the leg.

name: Tibial tuberosity
location: Rough projection on the anterior proximal tibia.
clues: Below the broad upper joint surfaces.
An anterior bump just below the knee.
function: Attachment site of the patellar ligament.

name: Medial malleolus
location: Medial projection at the distal tibia.
clues: Forms the inner ankle prominence.
Belongs to the tibia, not the fibula.
function: Contributes to the medial side of the ankle joint.

name: Fibula
location: Slender lateral bone of the leg.
clues: Much thinner than the tibia.
Its distal end forms the lateral malleolus.
sideTip: Keep the head proximal and the ankle end distal; its ankle joint surface faces medially toward the tibia.
function: Provides muscle attachment and contributes to ankle stability.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

name: Head of fibula
location: Expanded proximal end of the fibula.
clues: Upper end near the lateral knee.
Does not articulate directly with the femur.
function: Articulates with the proximal tibia.

name: Lateral malleolus
location: Distal expansion of the fibula.
clues: Forms the outer ankle prominence.
Belongs to the slender fibula.
function: Contributes to the lateral side of the ankle joint.

name: Calcaneus
location: Heel bone at the posterior foot.
clues: Largest bone of the ankle/heel region.
Forms the heel behind and below the other foot bones.
sideTip: The heel points posteriorly; the shelf-like projection supporting the talus is on the medial side.
function: Supports the heel and provides attachment for the Achilles tendon.

supplementarySources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb
